A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their text, equations, four figures, eighteen tables, and Appendices A–I are available and can be matched across pagination and formatting changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments evaluating and calibrating LLM-generated distributions on WGM, OpinionQA, and WVS, including subgroup and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including numerical comparisons of calibration, prompting, post-training, limited supervision, and held-out-dataset generalization.

M1.justification: The elicitation procedures and supervised regression followed by distribution normalization remain unchanged in Sections 3.2–3.6. The new explanation distinguishing output calibration from internal-weight alignment describes the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 92 questions from WGM, OpinionQA, and WVS, with the same demographics and held-out-dataset scenarios. v4's country-coverage and survey-language descriptions do not introduce new evaluations.

E2.justification: The same LLMs and comparison methods participate in the corresponding experiments, including standard, SD, CoT, five-shot, and log-probability comparisons. Newly cited works are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: The question-based 80/10/10 split, alignment metric, model configurations, elicitation settings, supervision sizes, and held-out-dataset procedures are unchanged. Appendix prompt templates also retain their substantive content.

E4.justification: The post-training, prompting, subgroup, generalization, and supervision-size analyses remain unchanged, including Appendices A–F. The new discussion of survey bias and temporal drift does not report additional tests.

E5.justification: Both retain ten random samples for limited-supervision experiments, three for five-shot prompting, and the same standard-deviation reporting and statistical tests. Appendix G and Table 14 retain the Bonferroni threshold and statistical results.

E6.justification: Numerical result entries in Tables 1–14 and the plotted results are unchanged. Both report the same 16.3% average alignment increase and improvement in 94.8% of settings in Section 4.2; qualitative experimental findings are also retained.

T1.justification: The opinion-alignment equation and regression formulation in Sections 3.4 and 3.6 are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs; the new limitations are informal qualifications.

C1.justification: The benchmark contribution, calibration benefits, subgroup variability, and limited-supervision claims are retained. The abstract and introduction make output-distribution alignment more explicit, consistent with the scope already established in v3.

C2.justification: v4 adds specific limitations concerning incomplete population coverage, surveys as imperfect ground truth, and temporal drift requiring recalibration and reevaluation. It replaces v3's explicit warning against replacing survey respondents with a broader warning against fully and correctly modeling human groups. Existing result interpretations remain intact.

D1.justification: Footnote 1 replaces the generic promise of code and data upon publication with a specified GitHub repository location. Release remains described in future tense. The hyperparameter grid and substantive implementation information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to Argyle, Cegin, Hayati, Jansen, Orlikowski, and Zheng and briefly expands application motivation and related-work coverage. The central positioning of supervised calibration relative to prior distributional-alignment research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized revisions clarify the abstract and introduction, expand Limitations, update acknowledgments, and correct wording and spelling. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 8–10 and 14 use shorter demographic or model labels and add abbreviation explanations, narrowing their displays. Table 3 moves between columns and surrounding material reflows. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v4 improves clarity about output-distribution calibration and adds useful qualifications about survey validity and temporal drift absent from v3. The planned repository location and tidier appendix tables also improve usability. Although the explicit warning against replacing survey respondents is softened, the expanded limitations provide a modest net gain in interpretive transparency; the empirical evidence remains unchanged.
